problem: The symbol on the left side of the shot-noise formula is missing: the text reads '_shot = 2q I_ph M² F(M) B' and ' = 2q I_ph M² F B'. A student sees a formula with no quantity on the left and cannot tell what is being computed.
fix: Write σ²_shot = 2q I_ph M² F(M) B in Section 2 (mean-square shot-noise current, unit A²), and repeat the same left-hand side in worked example step 5: σ²_shot = 2q I_ph M² F B = 1.16 × 10⁻¹⁴ A².

problem: The result is called simply 'SNR', but only shot noise was included; receiver thermal noise is ignored, and at M = 10 with a 1 GHz bandwidth thermal noise is usually larger than 108 nA. A student may carry away the wrong idea that this is the total SNR of an APD receiver.
fix: Label it 'shot-noise-limited SNR (thermal noise neglected)': SNR = I_M² / σ²_shot = (0.839 × 10⁻⁶)² / (1.16 × 10⁻¹⁴) = 60.7, i.e. 17.8 dB, and add one line saying the real SNR is lower once amplifier thermal noise is added.
